**My thinking, as I would work through it:**

I've been working this land for 40 years. I know what it needs. My 10.1 mu grows wheat over winter and then maize in summer on the same fields — that's how we've always done it here in Quzhou. My husband and I can manage this ourselves, though it gets harder at my age.

For wheat, I'll sow in early October after preparing the ground with the rotary machine — I hire someone with a tractor to do that. I buy improved seeds from the village supply store, the same variety I've used the last few years. I know it does well here. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer before sowing, then add urea in spring when the wheat starts shooting up. I water four times: once before sowing to get good germination, once before the ground freezes, once when jointing starts, and once when it heads out. I spray for weeds in winter and spray again around heading for rust and aphids. I expect around 450 jin per mu — that's a normal year for me.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant maize right away. I buy hybrid seed from the market — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has that's similar, I've used hybrid maize for many years now. I don't bother tilling again, it's too hot and too much work — I seed directly into the stubble. I fertilize in two goes and water when the crop looks stressed or when it's silking and it hasn't rained. Two sprays for weeds and corn borer. I expect around 550 jin per mu.
